question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold in the given sentence.

The elder's wisdom, gained from decades of experience, guided the young villagers through difficult times.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Knowledge.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Wisdom" means deep understanding and good judgment gained through experience. Its closest synonym is "Knowledge". (ज्ञान)
◦ Correct: The elder's wisdom (knowledge), gained from decades of experience, guided the young villagers through difficult times.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Foolishness" (lack of sense), Option 2 "Ignorance" (lack of knowledge) and Option 4 "Recklessness" (carelessness) are unrelated to deep understanding gained through experience.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of wisdom: knowledge, insight, sagacity, prudence, judgment, discernment. Antonyms: foolishness, ignorance, stupidity, folly.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Hapless (अभागा): Unfortunate (दुर्भाग्यशाली), Unlucky (बदकिस्मत), Luckless (अभागा), Ill-fated (दुर्भाग्यपूर्ण)

 

2. Indolent (आलसी): Lazy (आलसी), Idle (निठल्ला), Slothful (सुस्त), Lethargic (सुस्त)

 

3. Judicious (विवेकपूर्ण): Wise (बुद्धिमान), Prudent (विवेकपूर्ण), Sensible (समझदार), Sound (सुदृढ़)

 

4. Kindle (प्रज्वलित करना): Ignite (जलाना), Light (जलाना), Inflame (भड़काना), Arouse (जगाना)

 

5. Languish (क्षीण होना): Wither (मुरझाना), Weaken (कमजोर होना), Decline (क्षय होना), Waste away (क्षीण होना)

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Renounce
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Reject.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Renounce" means to formally give up a right, title, or belief. Its closest synonym among the options is "Reject" (to formally give up or refuse to accept). (त्याग करना)
◦ Example: The prince chose to renounce (reject) his claim to the throne and live as a monk.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Embrace" means to accept something willingly and enthusiastically — the opposite of giving something up.

 

• Option 2 "Accept" means to receive or agree to something willingly — contrary to the act of formally giving it up.

 

• Option 3 "Adopt" means to take up or start using something — it describes acquiring, not renouncing, something.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of renounce: reject, relinquish, abandon, forsake, disown, abdicate. Antonyms: embrace, accept, adopt, retain.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Malign (निंदा करना): Slander (निंदा करना), Defame (बदनाम करना), Vilify (बदनाम करना), Disparage (अपमानित करना)

 

2. Nostalgic (विगत स्मृतियों में लीन): Sentimental (भावुक), Wistful (उदासी भरी याद करने वाला), Reminiscent (स्मरण कराने वाला), Longing (तड़प भरा)

 

3. Opulent (समृद्ध): Luxurious (विलासितापूर्ण), Lavish (भव्य), Affluent (संपन्न), Sumptuous (शानदार)

 

4. Placid (शांत): Calm (शांत), Peaceful (शांतिपूर्ण), Serene (निर्मल), Tranquil (निश्चल)

 

5. Querulous (शिकायती): Complaining (शिकायती), Whiny (रोनेवाला), Peevish (चिड़चिड़ा), Fretful (बेचैन)

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold in the given sentence.

Dark clouds gathered over the hills, casting an ominous shadow over the village fair.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Threatening.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Ominous" means giving the impression that something bad is about to happen. Its closest synonym is "Threatening". (अशुभ संकेत देनेवाला)
◦ Correct: Dark clouds gathered over the hills, casting an ominous (threatening) shadow over the village fair.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 "Reassuring" (comforting), Option 3 "Promising" (hopeful) and Option 4 "Cheerful" (happy) are unrelated to a sense of impending danger or misfortune.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of ominous: threatening, menacing, foreboding, sinister, inauspicious. Antonyms: reassuring, promising, favorable, auspicious.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Rancor (द्वेष): Bitterness (कड़वाहट), Resentment (रोष), Animosity (शत्रुता), Hostility (शत्रुता)

 

2. Sagacious (बुद्धिमान): Wise (बुद्धिमान), Astute (चतुर), Shrewd (चालाक), Perceptive (सूक्ष्मदर्शी)

 

3. Taciturn (मितभाषी): Reserved (संकोची), Reticent (अल्पभाषी), Uncommunicative (अल्पभाषी), Silent (मौन)

 

4. Undermine (कमजोर करना): Weaken (कमजोर करना), Sabotage (विफल करना), Subvert (उलटना), Erode (क्षीण करना)

 

5. Vivacious (जीवंत): Lively (जीवंत), Animated (सजीव), Spirited (उत्साही), Sprightly (फुर्तीला)

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Dubiously
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Skeptically.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Dubiously" means in a manner showing doubt or hesitation. Its closest synonym among the options is "Skeptically" (with doubt or distrust). (संदेहपूर्वक)
◦ Example: She eyed the stranger's offer dubiously (skeptically), unsure whether to trust him.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Confidently" means with firm self-assurance — the opposite of hesitating in doubt.

 

• Option 3 "Assuredly" means certainly and without doubt — it conveys confidence rather than suspicion.

 

• Option 4 "Trustingly" means with full trust and no suspicion — directly contrary to the doubtful tone of dubiously.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of dubiously: skeptically, doubtfully, hesitantly, suspiciously, uncertainly. Antonyms: confidently, assuredly, certainly, trustingly.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Wary (सतर्क): Cautious (सतर्क), Careful (सावधान), Guarded (सतर्क), Vigilant (चौकस)

 

2. Zenith (चरम बिंदु): Peak (शिखर), Summit (शिखर), Apex (उच्च बिंदु), Pinnacle (शिखर)

 

3. Abhor (घृणा करना): Detest (घृणा करना), Loathe (नफरत करना), Despise (तिरस्कार करना), Hate (घृणा करना)

 

4. Buoyant (प्रफुल्लित): Cheerful (प्रसन्न), Optimistic (आशावादी), Light (हल्का), Resilient (लचीला)

 

5. Callous (निर्दयी): Insensitive (असंवेदनशील), Unfeeling (भावशून्य), Heartless (निर्दयी), Indifferent (उदासीन)

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold in the given sentence.

Losing his job triggered an existential crisis, forcing him to question the very purpose of his life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Philosophical.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Existential" means relating to human existence and its meaning or purpose. Its closest synonym is "Philosophical". (दार्शनिक)
◦ Correct: Losing his job triggered an existential (philosophical) crisis, forcing him to question the very purpose of his life.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Trivial" (unimportant), Option 2 "Physical" (bodily) and Option 4 "Superficial" (shallow) are unrelated to deep questions about the meaning and purpose of existence.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of existential: philosophical, ontological, metaphysical, fundamental. Antonyms: trivial, superficial, physical, material.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Diligent (परिश्रमी): Hardworking (मेहनती), Industrious (उद्यमी), Conscientious (कर्तव्यनिष्ठ), Assiduous (अध्यवसायी)

 

2. Elusive (मायावी): Evasive (टालमटोल करने वाला), Slippery (फिसलन भरा), Intangible (अमूर्त), Fugitive (भागने वाला)

 

3. Frivolous (तुच्छ): Trivial (तुच्छ), Silly (मूर्खतापूर्ण), Superficial (सतही), Petty (छोटा)

 

4. Gregarious (मिलनसार): Sociable (मिलनसार), Outgoing (मिलनसार), Convivial (मिलनसार), Companionable (साथी प्रेमी)

 

5. Hackneyed (घिसा-पिटा): Cliched (घिसा-पिटा), Trite (फीका), Overused (अत्यधिक प्रयुक्त), Stale (बासी)

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Pernicious
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Malicious.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Pernicious" means having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way. Its closest synonym among the options is "Malicious" (intending to cause harm). (हानिकारक)
◦ Example: The pernicious (malicious) rumors spread quietly through the office, damaging her reputation over months.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Beneficial" means producing good results — the direct opposite of causing gradual harm.

 

• Option 2 "Harmless" means not causing any damage — contrary to the destructive nature of pernicious.

 

• Option 3 "Wholesome" means conducive to health or well-being — the opposite of something subtly damaging.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of pernicious: harmful, injurious, damaging, malicious, deleterious, destructive. Antonyms: beneficial, harmless, wholesome, salutary.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Impervious (अभेद्य): Impenetrable (अभेद्य), Resistant (प्रतिरोधी), Unaffected (अप्रभावित), Immune (प्रतिरक्षित)

 

2. Jocular (विनोदी): Humorous (विनोदी), Playful (चंचल), Jovial (हंसमुख), Witty (हाज़िरजवाब)

 

3. Lament (विलाप करना): Mourn (शोक करना), Grieve (शोक मनाना), Bewail (विलाप करना), Bemoan (शोक व्यक्त करना)

 

4. Meager (अल्प): Scanty (अपर्याप्त), Sparse (विरल), Paltry (तुच्छ), Insufficient (अपर्याप्त)

 

5. Nimble (फुर्तीला): Agile (फुर्तीला), Quick (तेज़), Deft (निपुण), Sprightly (चुस्त)

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold in the given sentence.

The con artist managed to dupe several elderly residents out of their life savings.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Deceive.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Dupe" means to trick or deceive someone, often for personal gain. Its closest synonym is "Deceive". (धोखा देना)
◦ Correct: The con artist managed to dupe (deceive) several elderly residents out of their life savings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 "Console" (comfort), Option 3 "Admire" (respect) and Option 4 "Reward" (recompense) are unrelated to tricking or deceiving someone dishonestly.

 

NOTE

 

• "Dupe" is most often met in the phrase "dupe someone into (doing something)" — to trick someone into an action through deception. Synonyms: deceive, trick, fool, cheat, swindle, hoodwink. Antonyms: enlighten, undeceive, inform, guide.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Naive (भोला): Gullible (भोलाभाला), Innocent (निर्दोष), Unsuspecting (अनजान), Credulous (विश्वासी)

 

2. Candid (स्पष्टवादी): Frank (स्पष्ट), Honest (ईमानदार), Sincere (निष्कपट), Forthright (खरा)

 

3. Zealous (उत्साही): Ardent (उत्कट), Fervent (जोशीला), Passionate (भावुक), Enthusiastic (उत्साही)

 

4. Prudent (विवेकी): Wise (बुद्धिमान), Cautious (सतर्क), Judicious (न्यायसंगत), Sensible (समझदार)

 

5. Lucid (स्पष्ट): Clear (स्पष्ट), Coherent (सुसंगत), Transparent (पारदर्शी), Intelligible (समझने योग्य)

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Mythopoeic
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Myth-making.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Mythopoeic" means having the capacity to create myths, or relating to myth-making. Its closest synonym among the options is "Myth-making" (giving rise to new myths). (मिथक रचनेवाला)
◦ Example: The mythopoeic (myth-making) power of Tolkien's fiction gave modern readers an entirely new mythology.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Mythical" means existing only in myth or legend — it describes something imaginary, not the creative act of generating myths.

 

• Option 3 "Legendary" means very famous or celebrated, as in legend — it describes renown, not the process of myth-creation.

 

• Option 4 "Fabulous" means wonderful or extraordinary (originally 'like a fable') — in modern use it signals amazement, not myth-making.

 

NOTE

 

• "Mythopoeic" combines Greek "mythos" (story) and "poiein" (to make) and is most often used in literary criticism to describe works that generate their own mythology, as in "mythopoeic fiction". Synonyms: myth-making, myth-creating, legend-forming, fable-generating. Antonyms: realistic, factual, historical, documentary.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Ephemeral (क्षणभंगुर): Transient (अस्थायी), Fleeting (क्षणिक), Momentary (पल भर का), Short-lived (अल्पकालिक)

 

2. Sagacious (बुद्धिमान): Wise (बुद्धिमान), Astute (चतुर), Shrewd (चालाक), Perceptive (सूक्ष्मदर्शी)

 

3. Loquacious (बातूनी): Talkative (बातूनी), Garrulous (बकवादी), Voluble (वाक्पटु), Chatty (गपशप करने वाला)

 

4. Obdurate (हठी): Stubborn (जिद्दी), Inflexible (अनम्य), Adamant (दृढ़), Unyielding (न झुकने वाला)

 

5. Placate (शांत करना): Appease (संतुष्ट करना), Pacify (शांत करना), Soothe (सांत्वना देना), Mollify (नरम करना)

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold in the given sentence.

The boy admitted shamefacedly that he had broken his neighbor's window.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Embarrassedly.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Shamefacedly" means in a manner showing shame, guilt, or embarrassment. Its closest synonym is "Embarrassedly". (लज्जित होकर)
◦ Correct: The boy admitted shamefacedly (embarrassedly) that he had broken his neighbor's window.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Boldly" (fearlessly), Option 2 "Cheerfully" (happily) and Option 4 "Confidently" (assuredly) are unrelated to feeling shame or embarrassment.

 

NOTE

 

• "Shamefacedly" is most often used to describe someone's demeanor while confessing a fault, as in "to admit shamefacedly". Synonyms: embarrassedly, bashfully, sheepishly, guiltily, shyly. Antonyms: boldly, proudly, shamelessly, brazenly.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Contrite (पश्चातापी): Remorseful (पछतावा करने वाला), Repentant (पश्चातापी), Regretful (खेद युक्त), Penitent (प्रायश्चित करने वाला)

 

2. Meek (विनम्र): Docile (आज्ञाकारी), Humble (विनम्र), Submissive (अधीन), Timid (डरपोक)

 

3. Audacious (साहसी): Bold (साहसी), Daring (हिम्मती), Fearless (निडर), Brazen (ढीठ)

 

4. Furtive (चोरी-छिपे): Secretive (गुप्त), Stealthy (चुपके से), Sly (धूर्त), Clandestine (गुप्त)

 

5. Jubilant (हर्षित): Elated (प्रफुल्लित), Joyful (आनंदित), Ecstatic (अति आनंदित), Triumphant (विजयी)

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Dread
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Fear.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Dread" means intense fear or apprehension, especially about something that is about to happen. Its closest synonym among the options is "Fear" (a feeling of being afraid). (भय)
◦ Example: She felt a growing sense of dread (fear) as the exam results were about to be announced.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Hope" means a feeling of expectation and desire for a good outcome — the opposite of the apprehension found in dread.

 

• Option 2 "Joy" means a feeling of great happiness — an emotion of pleasure, not fear.

 

• Option 3 "Courage" means the ability to face danger without fear — it is the very opposite of the timidity implied by dread.

 

NOTE

 

• "Dread" is most often used in the phrase "live in dread of" — to constantly fear something. Synonyms: fear, apprehension, terror, dismay, trepidation. Antonyms: courage, confidence, fearlessness, comfort.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Apprehensive (आशंकित): Anxious (चिंतित), Worried (चिंतित), Uneasy (बेचैन), Nervous (घबराया हुआ)

 

2. Serene (शांत): Calm (शांत), Peaceful (शांतिपूर्ण), Tranquil (निर्मल), Placid (स्थिर)

 

3. Valiant (वीर): Brave (बहादुर), Courageous (साहसी), Heroic (वीरतापूर्ण), Gallant (शूरवीर)

 

4. Morose (उदास): Gloomy (उदास), Sullen (रूठा हुआ), Glum (निराश), Melancholy (खिन्न)

 

5. Elated (उल्लासित): Overjoyed (अत्यंत खुश), Thrilled (रोमांचित), Delighted (प्रसन्न), Exultant (विजयोल्लासित)

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold in the given sentence.

Guests were shown into the parlour to wait while tea was prepared.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Room.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Parlour" means a sitting room in a private house used for receiving visitors, or a shop providing a particular service. Its closest synonym is "Room". (कक्ष)
◦ Correct: Guests were shown into the parlour (room) to wait while tea was prepared.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 "Kitchen" (cooking area), Option 3 "Corridor" (passageway) and Option 4 "Basement" (underground floor) are unrelated to a sitting room meant for guests.

 

NOTE

 

• "Parlour" is most often seen today in compound terms like "beauty parlour" or "ice-cream parlour", referring to a shop offering a service. Synonyms: room, lounge, sitting-room, drawing-room, salon. Antonyms: exterior, outdoors, yard, courtyard.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Abode (निवास): Dwelling (निवास स्थान), Residence (आवास), Habitation (वास स्थान), Domicile (निवास)

 

2. Edifice (भवन): Building (इमारत), Structure (संरचना), Construction (निर्माण), Monument (स्मारक)

 

3. Threshold (दहलीज़): Doorway (द्वार), Entrance (प्रवेश द्वार), Doorsill (चौखट), Brink (कगार)

 

4. Spacious (विशाल): Roomy (बड़ा), Ample (पर्याप्त), Expansive (विस्तृत), Capacious (विशाल)

 

5. Secluded (एकांत): Isolated (पृथक), Remote (दूरस्थ), Private (निजी), Sheltered (आश्रित)

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Client
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Customer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Client" means a person or organisation that uses the professional services or advice of another. Its closest synonym among the options is "Customer" (one who purchases goods or services). (ग्राहक)
◦ Example: The law firm assigned a senior partner to handle its most important client (customer).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Employee" means a person hired to work for another — the opposite role of one who receives a service.

 

• Option 3 "Competitor" means a rival who contends for the same business or prize — not someone who uses one's services.

 

• Option 4 "Supervisor" means a person who oversees and directs others' work — a position of authority, not a service-user.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of client: customer, patron, consumer, buyer, purchaser. Antonyms: seller, vendor, provider, supplier.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Patron (संरक्षक): Sponsor (प्रायोजक), Benefactor (उपकारक), Supporter (समर्थक), Backer (समर्थक)

 

2. Vendor (विक्रेता): Seller (विक्रेता), Trader (व्यापारी), Merchant (सौदागर), Retailer (खुदरा विक्रेता)

 

3. Novice (नौसिखिया): Beginner (शुरुआती), Amateur (अव्यवसायी), Trainee (प्रशिक्षु), Learner (सीखने वाला)

 

4. Adept (निपुण): Skilled (कुशल), Proficient (दक्ष), Expert (विशेषज्ञ), Accomplished (सिद्धहस्त)

 

5. Diligent (मेहनती): Hardworking (परिश्रमी), Industrious (उद्यमी), Assiduous (लगनशील), Conscientious (कर्तव्यनिष्ठ)

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold in the given sentence.

He remained reticent about his plans, refusing to answer any questions from reporters.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Reserved.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Reticent" means not revealing one's thoughts or feelings readily; reluctant to speak about something. Its closest synonym is "Reserved". (अल्पभाषी)
◦ Correct: He remained reticent (reserved) about his plans, refusing to answer any questions from reporters.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Talkative" (chatty), Option 2 "Outgoing" (extroverted) and Option 4 "Sociable" (friendly) are unrelated to being reluctant to share one's thoughts.

 

NOTE

 

• "Reticent" is most often used in the phrase "reticent about (something)" — unwilling to talk about a particular topic. Synonyms: reserved, taciturn, secretive, uncommunicative, guarded, tight-lipped. Antonyms: talkative, outspoken, expansive, forthcoming.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Taciturn (मितभाषी): Silent (मौन), Uncommunicative (अल्पभाषी), Quiet (शांत), Withdrawn (अंतर्मुखी)

• Option 4 "Ancient" means belonging to the very distant past — describes age alone, not the layered, overwritten quality that defines palimpsestic.

 

NOTE

 

• "Palimpsestic" derives from "palimpsest", a manuscript scraped clean and reused while faint traces of the older text remain. Synonyms: layered, superimposed, overwritten, stratified. Antonyms: blank, unmarked, pristine.

• "Flair" is most often met in the phrase "a flair for" something, meaning a natural knack or stylish skill in that area. Synonyms: talent, aptitude, gift, knack, panache. Antonyms: ineptitude, incompetence, clumsiness.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Aptitude (योग्यता): Ability (क्षमता), Talent (प्रतिभा), Capability (सामर्थ्य), Proficiency (दक्षता)

 

2. Ineptitude (अयोग्यता): Incompetence (अक्षमता), Clumsiness (अनाड़ीपन), Inability (असमर्थता), Awkwardness (भद्दापन)

 

3. Panache (शान): Style (अंदाज़), Flamboyance (भड़कीलापन), Verve (जोश), Dash (जोश भरी शैली)

 

4. Novice (नौसिखिया): Beginner (शुरुआती), Amateur (अव्यवसायी), Learner (सीखनेवाला), Newcomer (नवागंतुक)

 

5. Prowess (निपुणता): Skill (कौशल), Expertise (विशेषज्ञता), Mastery (निपुणता), Dexterity (चपलता)

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Prophecy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Prediction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Prophecy" means a prediction of what will happen, especially one believed to be divinely inspired. Its closest synonym among the options is "Prediction" (a statement about the future). (भविष्यवाणी)
◦ Example: The old sage's prophecy (prediction) about the kingdom's fall came true many years later.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Confession" means an admission of wrongdoing or truth — it looks back at something already done, unlike a prophecy which foretells the future.

 

• Option 2 "Punishment" means a penalty imposed for an offence — a consequence for past actions, not a statement about what is yet to come.

 

• Option 3 "Explanation" means a statement that makes something clear — it clarifies the present or past, whereas a prophecy foretells the future.

 

NOTE

 

• "Prophecy" is most often met in the phrase "self-fulfilling prophecy" — a prediction that causes itself to become true. Synonyms: prediction, forecast, foretelling, augury, omen. Antonyms: hindsight, history, record.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Oracle (भविष्यवक्ता): Seer (दृष्टा), Prophet (पैगंबर), Soothsayer (भविष्यवक्ता), Visionary (दूरदर्शी)

 

2. Foreboding (आशंका): Premonition (पूर्वाभास), Apprehension (आशंका), Presentiment (पूर्वानुभूति), Dread (भय)

 

3. Retrospect (पूर्वदृष्टि): Hindsight (पूर्वदृष्टि से समझ), Recollection (स्मरण), Review (पुनरावलोकन), Reflection (चिंतन)

 

4. Ominous (अशुभ): Threatening (धमकी भरा), Sinister (अशुभ), Foreboding (आशंकाजनक), Menacing (डरावना)

 

5. Portent (अपशकुन): Omen (शकुन), Sign (संकेत), Warning (चेतावनी), Harbinger (अग्रदूत)

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold in the given sentence.

Torn between loyalty to his friend and telling the truth, he felt utterly aporetic about what to do next.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Conflicted.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Aporetic" means caught in a state of doubt or puzzlement, torn between conflicting views. Its closest synonym is "Conflicted". (द्विविधाग्रस्त)
◦ Correct: Torn between loyalty to his friend and telling the truth, he felt utterly aporetic (conflicted) about what to do next.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 "Confident" (self-assured), Option 3 "Decisive" (quick to decide) and Option 4 "Indifferent" (not caring either way) are unrelated to the inner doubt and pull between opposing views that the word describes.

 

NOTE

 

• "Aporetic" comes from the Greek "aporia", meaning a state of puzzlement or impasse. Synonyms: conflicted, perplexed, torn, doubtful, undecided. Antonyms: confident, certain, resolute, decisive.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Ambivalent (दुविधापूर्ण): Uncertain (अनिश्चित), Torn (द्विविधाग्रस्त), Undecided (अनिर्णीत), Wavering (डगमगाता हुआ)

 

2. Resolute (दृढ़ निश्चयी): Determined (दृढ़ निश्चयी), Firm (अटल), Steadfast (अडिग), Unwavering (अटूट)

 

3. Perplexed (हैरान): Confused (भ्रमित), Puzzled (चकित), Baffled (हतप्रभ), Bewildered (भौचक्का)

 

4. Nonchalant (लापरवाह): Indifferent (उदासीन), Unconcerned (निश्चिंत), Casual (लापरवाह), Composed (संयत)

 

5. Adamant (अड़ियल): Unyielding (न झुकनेवाला), Inflexible (अनम्य), Firm (दृढ़), Stubborn (हठी)

question:

Salubrious
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Wholesome.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Salubrious" means health-giving; favourable to physical well-being. Its closest synonym among the options is "Wholesome" (beneficial to health). (स्वास्थ्यप्रद)
◦ Example: The village was famous for its salubrious (wholesome) mountain air, which drew visitors seeking a cure for their ailments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Toxic" means poisonous and harmful to health — the direct opposite of the health-promoting quality that salubrious describes.

 

• Option 3 "Barren" means incapable of producing vegetation or life — this describes infertile land, not the healthful quality of a climate or place.

 

• Option 4 "Hazardous" means dangerous or risky — it signals a threat to safety, whereas salubrious signals benefit to health.

 

NOTE

 

• "Salubrious" is most often used to describe a "salubrious climate" — weather conditions that are good for one's health. Synonyms: wholesome, healthy, beneficial, invigorating, health-giving. Antonyms: unhealthy, toxic, noxious, insalubrious.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Noxious (हानिकारक): Harmful (हानिकारक), Poisonous (विषैला), Toxic (विषाक्त), Injurious (नुकसानदेह)

 

2. Invigorating (स्फूर्तिदायक): Refreshing (ताज़गी देनेवाला), Energizing (ऊर्जावान बनानेवाला), Bracing (स्फूर्तिदायक), Stimulating (उत्तेजक)

 

3. Pristine (अछूता): Unspoiled (अछूता), Pure (शुद्ध), Immaculate (निर्मल), Untouched (अछूता)

 

4. Fertile (उपजाऊ): Fruitful (फलदायी), Productive (उत्पादक), Rich (समृद्ध), Abundant (प्रचुर)

 

5. Malignant (घातक): Harmful (हानिकारक), Malicious (द्वेषपूर्ण), Dangerous (खतरनाक), Deadly (जानलेवा)

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold in the given sentence.

He continued to vacillate between the two job offers, changing his mind almost every day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Waver.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Vacillate" means to move indecisively between different opinions or actions. Its closest synonym is "Waver". (डगमगाना)
◦ Correct: He continued to vacillate (waver) between the two job offers, changing his mind almost every day.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Persist" (to continue firmly), Option 2 "Decide" (to make a firm choice) and Option 4 "Advance" (to move forward) are unrelated to the back-and-forth indecision that vacillate describes.

 

NOTE

 

• "Vacillate" is most often used in the phrase "vacillate between" two choices, showing indecision. Synonyms: waver, hesitate, dither, fluctuate, oscillate. Antonyms: decide, resolve, persist, commit.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Equivocate (अस्पष्ट बात करना): Hedge (टालमटोल करना), Prevaricate (बहानेबाजी करना), Waffle (अस्पष्ट बोलना), Temporize (समय टालना)

 

2. Deliberate (सोच-विचार करना): Ponder (विचार करना), Contemplate (चिंतन करना), Weigh (तौलना), Mull (सोचना)

 

3. Steadfast (अडिग): Loyal (वफादार), Unwavering (अटूट), Firm (दृढ़), Constant (स्थिर)

 

4. Procrastinate (टालमटोल करना): Delay (विलंब करना), Postpone (स्थगित करना), Stall (टालना), Defer (टालना)

 

5. Fluctuate (उतार-चढ़ाव होना): Vary (बदलना), Oscillate (दोलन करना), Swing (झूलना), Shift (परिवर्तित होना)

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Mindfulness
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Awareness.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Mindfulness" means the quality of being fully conscious and attentive, especially to the present moment. Its closest synonym among the options is "Awareness" (conscious perception of something). (सजगता)
◦ Example: Practising daily mindfulness (awareness) of her breathing helped her stay calm during stressful meetings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Carelessness" means lack of attention or thought — this is the direct opposite of the alert, conscious attention that mindfulness involves.

 

• Option 2 "Forgetfulness" means a tendency to forget things — a lapse of memory, which contrasts with the deliberate, present-moment attention of mindfulness.

 

• Option 3 "Anxiety" means a feeling of worry or unease — an emotional state, whereas mindfulness is a calm, deliberate state of attention, often practised to reduce anxiety.

 

NOTE

 

• "Mindfulness" is most often met in the phrase "mindfulness meditation" — a practice of focusing calmly on the present moment. Synonyms: awareness, attentiveness, consciousness, alertness, presence. Antonyms: carelessness, inattention, negligence, obliviousness.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Vigilant (सतर्क): Watchful (चौकस), Alert (सतर्क), Attentive (ध्यानशील), Wary (सावधान)

 

2. Oblivious (बेखबर): Unaware (अनजान), Unmindful (असावधान), Ignorant (अनभिज्ञ), Heedless (लापरवाह)

 

3. Introspective (आत्मनिरीक्षक): Reflective (चिंतनशील), Self-examining (आत्म-परीक्षण करनेवाला), Contemplative (मननशील), Thoughtful (विचारशील)

 

4. Serene (निर्मल): Calm (शांत), Peaceful (शांतिपूर्ण), Tranquil (प्रशांत), Placid (स्थिर)

 

5. Perceptive (सूक्ष्मदर्शी): Observant (अवलोकनशील), Insightful (अंतर्दृष्टिपूर्ण), Discerning (विवेकी), Sharp-eyed (तीक्ष्ण दृष्टि वाला)
